IN catalogum Argivorum heroum refert etiam Diome-
dem, Amphiaraum, inde mulieres, quas insignes inde
oriundas profert, ut est Alcmena, & Danae, hinc ad viros

Διομήδα.[?]) Quartum exemplum Diomedes non solum
heros fortissimus, sed in deorum numerum relatus est: nam
Thebano bello, quum Tydaeus pater Diomedis vulnera-
tus esset a Melanippo Thebano, aegerrime id ferens, roga-
uit Amphiaraum, ut occiso Melanippo, caput eius ad se
deferret, quo facto animum contuendo satiare non potuit,
quin caput denudatum carnibus, deuoraret carnes. Mi-
nerva etiam pro eo vulnere immortalitate Tydaeo com-
municauit: verum ob carnes Melanippi deuoratas, ea frui
non potuit, itaque rogauit deam, ut id munus filio Dio-
medi conferret, id quod Minerva fecit. Cultus est igitur
tanquam Deus cum Castore & Polluce: sic Polemon, I-
bycus, & Euripides in Meleagro testantur, referentibus
scholiis.

page.notes: Greek passages are transcribed as best read from the scan and are uncertain in several words; each doubtful word is marked [?]. The paragraph labels Διομήδα, Ταῦτα, Καὶ γυναικῶν and Πάλαι Ζεὺς are set in the text at paragraph start. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout; u/v and i/j are normalised (Argivorum, Jupiter, alii, ut, Minerva). The catchword "Argi-" stands alone at the right foot and is not repeated in the text.
